description:
FILED s513g (Opus, 2026-10-09); NOT fixed.  Found by the #2878 guard: Pl/t/facts-overlay-01.t row 5 (a module's own unit reading its overlay from the fixture root `Pl/t/lib`) passed under `./runpcl` and failed under the gate.

MECHANISM: the runtime spawns `perl -I d1 -I d2 ... pl2cl --module FILE` (`%p-transpile-inc-args`, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~25800).  In the gate, PCL_XSERVER is inherited (Pl/t/PCLCore.pm), so that pl2cl is a CLIENT that forwards the request to the test file's long-lived server -- which was started as `$^X $0 --xserver` with NONE of those -I switches.  pl2cl's own comment says it: "a caller that runs `perl -I<dir> pl2cl` would get a server without that -I.  No such caller sets PCL_XSERVER today" -- the runtime IS such a caller.  The module unit's `inc_paths` is therefore the server's, not the program's: a module under a `use lib` root that itself does `use Sibling` (Sibling in the same root) gets no prototype facts for Sibling in the gate, while `runpcl` / the sweep (no server) do -- the gate measures a different compiler state than production for exactly that shape.

#2878 sidesteps it for the overlay of a module's OWN unit by looking first in the root the module file itself was found in (Pl::Parser::register_unit_overlay).  The general fix belongs in pl2cl's client block: put the caller's -I list (perl's own switches, i.e. @INC minus the server's) in the socket KEY and in the request, as the comment already prescribes.  DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): a fixture pair A.pm (`use B; ... b { 1 }`) / B.pm (`sub b (&)`) under a `use lib` dir, run once under the gate harness and once with PCL_NO_SERVER=1.
subject: Under the gate's shared pl2cl server (PCL_XSERVER), a `pl2cl --module` the RUNTIME starts loses the runtime's -I list: the module unit is transpiled with the server's own search path, so a module's own `use Other` from a program's `use lib` dir is not found at transpile time
